spec.prompt: Inside the cramped Voskhod-2 capsule (first reference), weightless, March 1965. Close-up of the bare right hand of the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov (face and suit exactly as in his reference images), the white sleeve of his Berkut suit with its rust-orange cuff visible, drawing on a small cream card held flat against a log book on his knee. The card is almost finished and clearly shows the drawing in the second reference: the drawing is small and loose on a small cream landscape card, with wide blank margins, mostly in the left and middle of the card: one sweeping, slightly curved diagonal band rising from the lower left to the upper right, made of soft, loose coloured-pencil strokes that run along the band; from its outer (upper) edge inward: a broad black band, a thin light-blue band, a yellow band, a thin orange-red line with a small red ball of the sun sitting on it near the middle of the band, then several layered blues below (light blue to deep blue) whose strokes fray out at the lower edge. No Earth disc, no black background, no text, no stars, no spacecraft, no signature. His pencils are the short Soviet 'Taktika' coloured pencils from a flat blue-and-white cardboard box (as in the full photo reference): each pencil is tied with a thin white cotton thread, the threads gathered to a small ring of green-coated wire: his glove is off, and on his bare wrist, just beyond the plain silver-grey glove ring of the sleeve, sits a thin loop of green-coated wire; four or five short pencils float around his hand on their white threads tied to that loop, drifting slowly in zero gravity. With a red pencil he gently colours the small red ball of the sun on the band, then lifts the pencil away and the finished drawing is fully visible. High angle looking down onto his knee: the card faces the camera and fills the centre of the frame, the whole drawing clearly readable and never covered by his hand for long. Warm light from a porthole, the instrument panel soft and out of focus behind. Photorealistic, shot on 35mm film, IMAX documentary realism in the spirit of Apollo 11 (2019) and Gravity. Accurate 1965 Soviet hardware: the white Berkut spacesuit with rust-orange harness straps, a white helmet with red CCCP letters above the visor, Soviet markings only. Hard directional sunlight, deep black space, crisp silhouettes. No on-screen text, no captions.
